papers.title: LongSpec: Long-Context Lossless Speculative Decoding with Efficient Drafting and Verification
papers.abstract: LongSpec provides lossless speculative decoding for long-context large language model inference. It uses a memory-efficient draft model with a constant-sized KV cache, position indices for the training-inference mismatch, and efficient tree attention. Experiments report up to 3.26x speedup over Flash Attention baselines and lower wall-clock time for reasoning workloads.

papers.title: HCSpec: Two-Tier Horizontal Cascade Speculative Decoding for High-Efficiency Large Language Model Inference
papers.abstract: HCSpec proposes heterogeneous position-specialized draft modules for speculative decoding. Evaluation on Qwen and Llama models reports 15-30% higher end-to-end speedup than EAGLE-3 and up to 3.72x acceleration over autoregressive decoding across multiple tasks and inference configurations.

papers.title: UniSpec: Training-Free Speculative Decoding for Robust LLM Acceleration Across Languages and Hardware
papers.abstract: UniSpec is a training-free lossless speculative decoding framework with device-aware draft-size calibration, confidence-based candidate retention, and tree expansion. Experiments across languages, model architectures and hardware report up to 2.6x speedup with identical output quality and provide code and a benchmark.

papers.title: SpecCache: Speculative KV Cache Reuse for Efficient RAG Serving
papers.abstract: SpecCache addresses high prefill latency in long-context RAG serving for large language models. It uses deep-layer features from a lightweight speculative model to select critical tokens for target-model KV cache recomputation. The authors report 2.17-3.95x lower time-to-first-token and 2.7-5.2x higher inference throughput with negligible quality degradation.

papers.title: EQUIP: EQUivariant preserving In-Place updates for Efficient Token Pruning
papers.abstract: EQUIP optimizes token pruning for large language model inference through in-place KV cache replacement, cached rotary position operations and re-indexing. Evaluation reports CPU and GPU speedups over StreamingLLM and H2O, and up to 4.18x CPU and 2.61x GPU speedup when combined with Paged Attention.

papers.title: PDTrim: Targeted Pruning for Prefill-Decode Disaggregation in Inference
papers.abstract: PDTrim integrates model pruning with prefill-decode disaggregated LLM inference. It analyzes stage-specific pruning sensitivity and removes different blocks for prefill and decode, with evaluation in both disaggregated serving and unified deployment settings.

papers.title: Theory-optimal Quantization Based on Flatness
papers.abstract: This work studies activation outliers in post-training quantization for large language models and proposes Bidirectional Diagonal Quantization. Experiments report less than 1% accuracy drop for W4A4 on Llama-3-8B and improved low-bit accuracy for a 70B reasoning model.

papers.title: OCP: Outlier-Centric Probing for Dynamic Structured Pruning of LLMs
papers.abstract: OCP provides hardware-friendly dynamic structured pruning for efficient LLM inference using sensitivity-weighted FFN probing, attention-accumulated probing and adaptive layer sparsity. Experiments on Llama and OPT report up to 25% perplexity reduction at 1.6x speedup.

papers.title: From Local to Global: Revisiting Structured Pruning Paradigms for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: GISP is an iterative global structured pruning method for hardware-friendly LLM inference. It removes attention heads and MLP channels with loss-based importance, produces nested subnetworks for prune-once deploy-many operation, and evaluates task-aligned calibration across Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek and Qwen models.

papers.title: OjaKV: Context-Aware Online Low-Rank KV Cache Compression
papers.abstract: OjaKV combines high-fidelity anchor tokens with online low-rank KV cache compression for long-context LLM inference. The projection adapts during prefill and decode, remains compatible with FlashAttention, and is evaluated under high compression ratios and distribution shifts.

papers.title: Prune as You Generate: Online Rollout Pruning for Faster and Better RLVR
papers.abstract: ARRoL reduces distributed training cost for large language models trained with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. It prunes low-value rollouts inside the inference engine and performs dynamic batching of survivors for policy updates. Across Qwen and Llama workloads it reports up to 1.7x training speedup while improving average accuracy.

papers.title: ZoomR: Memory Efficient Reasoning through Multi-Granularity Key Value Retrieval
papers.abstract: ZoomR targets long-output reasoning for large language models with adaptive summary compression and hierarchical KV cache retrieval. Experiments on math and reasoning workloads report competitive quality while reducing inference memory requirements by more than 4x.
